title: Giving
hookLine: a steady portion for the Church and the poor
tomorrow: can a lazy afternoon be part of a holy life?

lines: HE SAT AND WATCHED THE GIVING.
cards: A first paycheck lands, and it's smaller than the hours felt. Taxes took a bite. The rest is spoken for before it arrives: the phone bill, gas, the thing sitting in a cart.
So how much of it is actually yours, and how much is yours to give? Mark tells about a day Jesus sat down across from the temple treasury and watched people give. Rich people put in a lot.
Then a poor widow walks up with two small coins.

teach.b: Jesus calls his disciples over and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Amen I say to you, this poor widow hath cast in more than all they who have cast into the treasury." More than all of them.
Mark gives the reason: they gave out of their abundance, and she gave out of her want.
In this story, Jesus measures the share, not the size. That's the heart of a portion.
Paul adds the how, writing to the church at Corinth: "Every one as he hath determined in his heart, not with sadness, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver."
Determined in his heart: decided ahead of time, not whatever's left at the end of the month.

One to tell a friend: helping the Church with its material needs is one of the Church's precepts, the short list of basics the Church asks of Catholics, and the Catechism adds, each according to his own ability.
A student's portion and a surgeon's portion look different, and both count.
So a rule for life names a portion: some for the parish, some for the poor, set before the spending starts, and given steadily, not just when a sad story goes viral.

how: Catholics support their parish through the Sunday collection or regular online giving, and give to the poor through parish collections, Catholic charities and their own neighbors.

o: a large one-time gift to a well-known cause
the leftover money at the end of the month
a steady share for the Church and the poor

games.q: the widow's coins — tap the pairs.

s: Jesus praised the rich givers because their gifts were largest
he said the widow cast in more than all: they gave from abundance, she from her want.
helping the Church with its material needs is one of the Church's precepts
each according to his own ability, the Catechism says.
the Church sets one fixed amount every Catholic must give
no number is set; Paul says as he hath determined in his heart.

games.q: your roommate gives a big amount whenever a sad story goes viral, then nothing for months. she asks what you think. what fits Paul?
o: big bursts are better; what matters is the total over the year.
she should stop, since giving from emotion doesn't count.
decide a steady share ahead of time, and give it gladly.
games.why: Paul says as he hath determined in his heart, not of necessity: decided ahead, steady, and cheerful.

practice: Take one coin or bill from your wallet and hold it, or picture the last amount that landed in your account. Look at it the way Jesus looked at two small coins.
Decide your portion now, a share and not a leftover, and where it goes: the parish, a food bank, someone you know who's short this month.

wordCard.voice: Giving. A steady portion, decided in the heart ahead of time, for the Church and the poor, given gladly.

orig.note: Greek: cheerful, glad. the word in 'God loveth a cheerful giver'.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: a portion, measured by the share, the way the widow's was. Until tomorrow.
